title: fix(plugin-security): Layer 0 no longer walls a federated object with a phantom organization_id (#7835)
body:
Part of #7835

Fixes the **tenant** half of the card. The ownership half is out of this lane's file surface and is filed as #7858 with its measurement — see "What this PR does not do".

## What was measured

The card asked for a boot, and named two conditions under which "latent, no change needed" would be the right answer. Both were measured on a real showcase boot through `@objectstack/verify` at `origin/main` @ `b54aaab`. Neither holds, and one of the card's own mechanism claims is falsified:

**1. The wildcard `tenant_isolation` RLS policy really is retired — and that does not make the card latent, it makes it unconditional.** ADR-0095 D1 (not ADR-0090 D1) retired it from every shipped permission set and moved the tenant wall to **Layer 0**, `tenant-layer.ts`, AND-composed ahead of business RLS. Layer 0 needs no policy to fire: under a walled posture it emits an `organization_id` predicate for any object whose field set carries that column. So the card's framing — "a compiled wildcard rule *would* add a second predicate" — describes a mechanism that no longer exists, while the defect it predicted is live on every federated read.

**2. The registry injects a phantom `organization_id` into federated objects.** `applySystemFields` adds the platform anchors to every object that has not opted out, federated ones included, while `Engine.syncObjectSchema` returns early for `external != null` and issues no DDL — the remote schema is owned externally. Measured on the shipped showcase:

```
showcase_ext_customer  external={"remoteName":"customers","writable":false}
  registered fields: organization_id, created_at, created_by, updated_at,
                     updated_by, owner_id, owning_business_unit_id,
                     name, email, region, lifetime_value
  remote table `customers` columns: name, email, region, lifetime_value
```

**3. The predicate reaches the query.** `security.getReadFilter('showcase_ext_customer', ctx)` under `isolated` returned `{"organization_id":"org_alpha"}`; under `group` with a membership set, `{"organization_id":{"$in":[...]}}`; under `group` with none, the deny sentinel. End to end on the real REST stack under a walled posture, `GET /api/v1/data/showcase_ext_customer` answered **HTTP 200 with zero rows**.

That is the card's fail-open/fail-closed pair in one observation: the wall isolates nothing, and the federated catalog stops answering the moment a deployment turns the organization wall on.

## Dialect

Every filter-shape assertion in this PR is **dialect-free by construction** — it asserts the `FilterCondition` plugin-security composes, before any driver sees it. Only the end-to-end case is dialect-bound, and it ran on **SQLite** (the showcase's external datasource), which is the dialect where the defect is invisible: an unresolvable identifier degrades to a string literal, so the comparison is constant-false rather than an error. Postgres and MySQL raise `column "organization_id" does not exist` instead. No Postgres/MySQL run was performed; the filter-shape cases are what carry the claim across dialects.

## The fix

Layer 0 asks "is this a tenant object?" by asking whether the object carries `organization_id`. It is now told the truth for a federated object: an anchor the platform injected into storage it does not own is not a column.

The test is **provenance, not `external != null`**. A federated object may legitimately expose a real remote tenant column by declaring it, and suppressing its wall would delete one that works. `federated-phantom-anchors.ts` compares the registered field definition against the shipped `TENANT_SCOPE_FIELD_DEF` that `applySystemFields` spreads verbatim — the same discipline `platform-tenant-policies.ts` records for ADR-0105 finding F1 and `platform-ownership-policies.ts` for #5492. Any inexact match answers "not the platform's anchor" and leaves the wall in place: the fail direction is toward isolation.

Unchanged, and pinned as such: local objects, a federated object with an author-declared `organization_id`, and Layer 1 — an app-authored policy still reaches the compiler untouched (ADR-0049).

**The card's first fence is respected**: #7833's engine-level skip is not widened and `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` is not touched. Layer 0 is a `where` predicate composed into the query AST, not a driver option, so the engine fix could not have reached it anyway.

## Reverse verification — predictions written before the mutations

Recorded first, then run. Both matched.

**Ablation A** — drop the guard at the Layer 0 call site:

| pin | predicted | actual |
|:--|:--|:--|
| federated + injected anchor, `isolated` | RED | RED |
| federated + injected anchor, `group` | RED | RED |
| federated + author-declared `organization_id` | GREEN | GREEN |
| LOCAL object | GREEN | GREEN |
| dogfood: federated read composes no org predicate | RED | RED |
| dogfood: LOCAL control still walled | GREEN | GREEN |
| dogfood: end-to-end rows survive | RED | RED |

Two further cases went red that the prediction table had not itemized — "federated with no active org" and "an authored policy still reaches the compiler" — both in the same direction, since without the fix Layer 0 composes into those results too. Reported rather than back-filled into the table.

**Ablation B** — drop the provenance half, so every federated object counts as phantom: exactly one pin red, "federated object whose AUTHOR DECLARED a real remote `organization_id`: the wall STAYS". Predicted, and it is what stops the provenance test from being decoration.

## Tests

`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/federated-tenant-layer0.test.ts` proves the **decision** (dialect-free, hand-built field sets). Because its fixtures build the injected anchor themselves, it cannot also prove the registry still produces one — expectation and reality would share a source. `packages/qa/dogfood/test/federated-rls-injectors.dogfood.test.ts` is the independent witness: a real boot, the real registry, the shipped federated object, plus a LOCAL control so the pin cannot pass by the wall being switched off everywhere. That file went red against the pre-fix build and green after — the before/after quoted above.

## What this PR does not do

- **Ownership scoping (`__readScope` own/unit lowered to an `owner_id` predicate).** Measured and confirmed firing on a federated object without the ADR-0090 grandfather stamp — `{"owner_id":"usr_member_1"}` against a table with no such column. The scope label is stamped in plugin-security, but the predicate is built in `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, outside this card's declared surface, so it is reported and filed as **#7858** rather than patched here. This is why the first line reads `Part of`.
- **The root cause.** All three fixes so far — the engine's, this one, and the one #7858 proposes — are consumers re-deriving "that column is not really there" about the same producer, `applySystemFields`. Discussed in #7858; a registry-level answer is a larger change than any of these cards scoped.
